subject: Request: SLA remediation for rolling authorization timeouts during PromoOps window
messages:
From: Matt Turner <matt.turner@cardspring.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Alvarez <sara@cardspring.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Rolling authz timeouts during PromoOps window — urgent impact

Jasmine,

We experienced a sustained set of authorization timeouts starting ~08:45 PDT and lasting in waves until ~10:05. This happened during our PromoOps surge (traffic ~3x baseline) and directly affected checkout conversions — we saw a ~12% drop in auth-success events during the window.

Prelim details:
- Scope: card auth / tokenization calls routed to your us-west-2 cluster
- Error pattern: 504 / internal auth timeout, intermittent 429s when retries piled up
- First observed: 2028-04-09 08:45:21 PDT
- Last observed (initial): 2028-04-09 10:05:02 PDT

Attaching our aggregated logs and span traces. We need confirmation of whether this meets SLO downtime criteria and, if so, next steps for a remedy/credit. Our renewal review is next week so a timely answer would be appreciated.

Attachments: promoop_logs_20280409.txt, promoop_trace_20280409.zip

Thanks,
Matt Turner
Head of Payments Engineering
CardSpring
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Turner <matt.turner@cardspring.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling authz timeouts during PromoOps window — urgent impact

Matt — thanks for the heads up and the attachments. I’m escalating to our SRE and SLO team (cc: Kimberly, David). Quick answers up front:

1) We will verify the availability window against the contractual SLOs for your tier (Committed throughput + 99.9% availability for auth endpoints).
2) We’ll pull server-side traces and compute the confirmed impact window; can you confirm whether the attached logs contain all client-side attempts including retries? If you have the raw request IDs or a sample request id (x-request-id) that hit 504s, include those and we’ll correlate.
3) We’ll target a preliminary impact verification within 24 hours and provide a reconciliation packet for credit eligibility.

For the immediate triage: Kimberly, can you pick this up for the us-west-2 auth cluster? David — please prepare the availability calc and an initial telem extract.

Matt — I’ll follow up by EOD with next steps and whether we need any more artifacts (e.g., SLA claim form signed).

—Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
From: Matt Turner <matt.turner@cardspring.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Alvarez <sara@cardspring.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 09:43:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling authz timeouts during PromoOps window — urgent impact

Jasmine / team —
Thanks. Confirming the logs include client attempts + retry metadata; I highlighted three representative x-request-ids in the attached text file (lines 112, 374, 981). We also exported a lightweight metrics snapshot (attached) showing auth success vs failures by minute.

If helpful: we observed a fast increase in queuing latency just before the first 504; retry storms started around 08:50 and amplified failures. Happy to hop on a call if it helps.

-Matt

Attachments: promoop_logs_20280409.txt (includes sample ids), sla_claim_form_cardspring.pdf
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt Turner <matt.turner@cardspring.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling authz timeouts during PromoOps window — urgent impact

Team — quick triage notes after correlating CardSpring sample ids with service traces:
- Confirmed request path: auth proxy -> tokenization service (svc-token) -> third-party PSP adaptor
- Observed consistent increase in svc-token queue wait time from 08:46:12 to 09:58:45 PDT; median queue wait jumped from ~12ms to ~430ms.
- Several worker processes experienced GC spikes and a small set of GPU/CPU contention events tied to an autoscaler oscillation (scale-out + rapid scale-in) in the us-west-2 auth pool.

Prelim SLO implication: We have a contiguous window of elevated error rates and latency between 08:46:00 and 09:58:45. I will hand the raw telemetry and the computed availability delta to David for formal eligibility math.

Next steps:
- David: compute affected request volume and % availability loss vs the SLO baseline (CardSpring committed throughput).
- Laura: please book a 60-min postmortem invite with CardSpring for tomorrow; include SRE, Product, and Account team.
- Jasmine: confirm the list of artifacts to attach to the customer packet (telemetry bundle, raw traces, kubernetes event dump, autoscaler logs).

I’ll prepare an internal RCA draft once we have full telemetry from the autoscaler and kernel metrics.

—Kimberly
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Matt Turner <matt.turner@cardspring.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Rolling authz timeouts during PromoOps window — urgent impact

Matt — thank you for the patience. Summary and next steps below.

Summary of verification:
- Confirmed impact window: 2028-04-09 08:46:12 PDT -> 2028-04-09 09:58:45 PDT (per server-side traces).
- Computed availability impact vs committed SLO: 99.65% during the affected window for auth endpoints (CardSpring tier SLO = 99.9%). This meets the threshold for SLO remediation consideration.
- Root cause (prelim): autoscaler instability led to transient worker shortages and request queuing; GC & resource contention amplified tail latency.

Customer packet and remediation path:
- Artifacts included: promoop_trace_20280409.zip, promoop_logs_20280409.txt, server_event_dump_usw2_20280409.tar.gz (attached to internal packet), computed availability matrix.
- Credit eligibility: Based on the contract, we will propose a proportional credit for the impacted period. David will compute the pro-rata credit amount and Jasmine (me) will send the formal credit letter.
- Postmortem: Cookbook session scheduled: 2028-04-11 09:00 PDT — 60 minutes (invite sent). Please join: SRE, Product, CardSpring Eng, Account.

Action items for CardSpring: please review and sign the attached SLA claim form (sla_claim_form_cardspring.pdf) so we can process the credit. If you want an immediate bridge call, we can do 30 minutes today.

We’ll continue the RCA and will follow up with a final postmortem within 72 hours.

—Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Enterprise Success
Redwood Inference
